_what: Differences between src/workingset/model.py and interactive/src/*.js that are known, measured and explained. CI is green on this set and red on anything else. An entry is a DEBT, not a decision: it records that the two implementations disagree and why we believe they do, never that the disagreement is correct. Delete an entry when the difference is fixed - the test ASSERTS that every entry matched something, so a stale allowlist fails the build.

_fields.quantity: vectors.json out-key, exact or with a trailing * as a prefix glob
_fields.where: matches the vector's state fields, the derived n_gpu / replicas, and the vector's cond block under a _ prefix (_duty, _sla_headroom, _sla10_headroom, _warm_p5, _decode_ceiling, _ctx_cv2, _steady_cap_ratio, _sla_f_unreachable). Values: a literal, a list, or {gt|gte|lt|lte|ne|nin}. An entry with NO where and max_rel 1.0 pins nothing at all - relErr is bounded by 1 for any finite pair - so every entry here is gated on the condition that causes it. Use _sla10_headroom, not _sla_headroom, for the quantities compared at the hard-wired 10 s budget.
_fields.observed_rel: the worst relative error actually measured on 2026-09-07, 821 vectors / 46,797 comparisons
_fields.max_rel: the ceiling this entry buys; a known 4% difference must not license a 40% one

_measured_at: 2026-09-07, tests/golden/vectors.json schema 1, 821 vectors, against src/workingset/model.py with steady_decode_point capped at the GPU-resident population on both sides. 515 comparisons were allowlisted before the cap; 165 are now, and steady_saturated needs no entry at all.

entries.hypothesis: SATURATED ON BOTH SIDES, and both say so: past the cap each side reports n = floor(its own GPU-resident warm p95), and the two p95 draws come from different samplers (numpy vs mulberry32) at different iteration counts. The residual is that draw difference, worst on small populations (9 against 10 is 11%). 132 states at ratio >= 1, the flag identical on every one - which is why steady_saturated needs no entry.
aggregate/n at each side's own floor(p95); same cap-draw residual as steady_n

INSIDE the resident cap the same two algorithms disagree by a bounded amount: Python bisects integer n redrawing contexts at every probe, the explorer inverts a LINEAR interpolation of one pre-sampled aggregate. 45 of 821 states, worst 18%, no trend in _steady_cap_ratio below 1 - so this is the algorithmic residue, not the cap.
same bounded interpolation-vs-bisection residue as steady_n

d_d divides the output demand by decode_users_group x floor, and both sides bisect that ceiling on their own sampled curve. On a configuration whose ceiling is a few dozen sequences they land one apart, and one step of thirty is a thirtieth of the capacity. THE DEFAULT-FLOOR SLICE, kept at the ceiling it had before power_draw's floor bug was fixed: nothing in that fix touches a floor-40 state, so this entry must not move. 7 states, worst 4.2%.

the same integer-bisection noise, at the floors the slider reaches away from 40, where it is far larger: a low floor puts the decode ceiling in the single digits, and one step of three is a third of the capacity. Gated on the ceiling as well as the floor, since the ceiling is the cause and the floor only selects for it; 45 is the largest ceiling that exhibits it, and above that the quantity is inside its band everywhere. Replaces the pre-fix `decode_floor != 40` entry, which licensed 87.5% on any state at any ceiling: the floor is a power_draw parameter now, so the two sides price the same cap and only the ceiling's own noise is left. 14 states, worst 33%.

the electricity line is power_kw x 720 x eur_kwh, so it inherits the small-ceiling noise above one-for-one, diluted by the flat host_w adder. energy_total_month does not fail: the hardware line dominates the bill. 2 states, worst 10.4%.

d_d is clamped to what prefill leaves, min(max(0, 1 - d_p), ...), and d_p is itself clamped at 1. At rho = 0.9996 the two samplers land on opposite sides of that clamp: one side has 3.6e-4 of the machine left for decode and the other exactly none.

ILL-CONDITIONED at the cliff, not a formula difference: lam = k/(a + k b) with k = 2(SLA - E[S|miss]), and these are configurations whose miss alone eats 95-100% of its own TTFT budget (almost all Mistral-Medium-3.5, whose 88 full-attention layers make a miss cost ~10 s against a 10 s SLA). k is then the difference of two nearly equal sampled numbers and passes through zero, where Python returns a hard 0 and the mirror returns 1.5 users. The window is bounded on BOTH sides so a state arbitrarily past its SLA is not admitted.

the same 1/k amplification, away from the cliff and therefore bounded: a relative difference in E[S|miss] enters lam multiplied by roughly SLA/(SLA - c) = 1/headroom, so at a headroom of 0.15-0.75 a 2% moment difference reads as 3-13%. Seven states of 821, all inside that window; above 0.75 headroom the quantity is inside its band everywhere.

ILL-CONDITIONED: the Pollaczek-Khinchine wait carries 1/(1 - rho), which is ~2,700 at the rho = 0.9996 the worst state sits at, so a 0.04% difference in E[S] between the two samplers decides whether the queue has a steady state at all - one side returns 939 s and the other Infinity. The closed forms match term for term.
same 1/(1 - rho) amplification at rho = 0.9996
B* = SLA (1 - rho) / E[S|miss] is LINEAR in (1 - rho), so at rho = 0.9996 one side reads 6.6e-4 bursts and the other clamps to 0
B x E[S|miss] / (1 - rho); same amplification, and the same Infinity-vs-finite split at rho = 0.9996
f* = (1/rate - warm)/(cold - warm); at rho ~ 1 the numerator is a difference of two nearly equal numbers, so f* lands at 3.1e-4 against 1.4e-4 - both meaning 'this configuration is already saturated'

ILL-CONDITIONED AT THE ZERO TEST, which both sides now run the same way: is the WHOLE mean TTFT at f = 0 - the all-warm queue wait plus the miss's own prefill - already past the budget? All 20 states sit in the first quarter of this entry's window: their _sla10_headroom, which the fixture records per vector, reads 0.007-0.013. A hair of sampling difference in the moments decides which side of the cliff they land: Python reads 0 and the mirror 6e-4, agreeing in meaning and not in value. The window is bounded on BOTH sides so a state arbitrarily past its budget is not admitted.

the same 1/k amplification max_users_latency has: f* solves a linear equation whose coefficient is k = 2(SLA - E[S|miss]), so a couple of percent of sampling difference in the miss cost becomes tens of percent in f* once the miss eats most of the budget. Four states, headroom 0.10-0.30; above 0.35 headroom this quantity is inside its band everywhere.

E[S^2] on a miss is essentially the FOURTH moment of the context length, and its sampling variance grows steeply with the context's squared coefficient of variation. Every state past it comes from the heavy-tailed decile (fixture p90 of _ctx_cv2 is 0.97); 200,000 Python draws against the explorer's 20,000 is not enough there.
the P-K wait is lam E[S^2] / (2(1 - rho)), so it inherits E[S^2]'s heavy-tail sampling error one-for-one
queue wait + the hit's own prefill; the wait term carries E[S^2] and the same heavy-tail error

two independent integer bisections on a sampled monotone curve. At a ceiling of ONE the relative error is 1 by definition: it says one side's single decoder just clears the floor and the other's just misses it. Every failing state has a ceiling of 23 or below; above that the two agree inside the band.

a COUNT of two to nine sessions (Mistral-Medium-3.5 on narrow topologies), where one session either way is 12-33%, PLUS the standing approximation: the explorer scales warm p5 by (1 - p_sub) where Python counts user-class sessions inside each fill. The approximation is invisible at ordinary counts and rounds badly at two.

the same tiny-count effect on the raw p5. Both sides take the p5 of an integer-valued fill; at a count of two nothing else can be expected of them. The bands for this quantity and max_users_cache are already derived with these states excluded (see mc_spread.excluded_from_bands), so this entry is the tail that exclusion names.

SIGN-STABLE SAMPLER-STRUCTURE BIAS, not a state-dependent one, which is why this entry has no `where`: the mirror reads 5-7% LOW on every one of the 30 states past the band and never high. decodeCurves draws one context pool per iteration and reads it cumulatively (common random numbers across n) where decode_curves redraws per n, and at n = 1 the per-user speed is a median of 1/(a + b L) on a single draw - the most tail-sensitive statistic compared, hardest under FP16 KV where the sampled term dominates the step. decode_p50_n8 and _n64, the same estimator once the average over n contexts washes the structure out, stay inside their bands everywhere; that is the evidence for this reading rather than a formula difference.
